summary: Kittitas County site: 1933 camp, L-4 cab built 1935, abandoned around 1966; footings and anchors remain on a one-mile old-road hike.

facts.status_note: The register says the lookout was abandoned in 1966 and is no longer standing; FireLookout.com also lists it as gone.

staffing.status: last staffing found: lookout-fireman B. D. March, 1933

access.note: Directions run from the North Fork Teanaway Road to the Stafford Creek Road (9703) on Wenatchee National Forest land; WillhiteWeb says high clearance is best and the road can be walked.

visit.trail_note: WillhiteWeb gives one mile one-way with 700 feet of gain. A 2020 trip report describes it as an old road leading to the old lookout site. Nothing is left to climb.

events.note: B. D. March named as Stafford Creek lookout-fireman; WillhiteWeb says the site was a camp unless an earlier structure existed

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and FireLookout.com use Stafford. WillhiteWeb says some inventories mistakenly call the site Standup Ridge Lookout, so the story uses Stafford.

notes_for_editor: Dates agree across the register, FireLookout.com and WillhiteWeb for the 1935 build and the 1966 abandonment. WillhiteWeb's Leavenworth newspaper item places B. D. March at the site in 1933, before the cab; the story calls the site a camp then, as WillhiteWeb does. The 1934 panoramas also predate the cab, consistent with that camp history. The 2020 trip report is a single hiker's account and is cited only for the route. The most recent visit described is WillhiteWeb's October 2021 trip. The brief's 1935 build and 2020 registration both checked out. Access level 'public' is inferred from forest roads and a published trailhead; no closure was found.
